From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package materially departs from the Buyer playbook on liability, disclosure, knowledge, completion protection and several identified diligence matters. The most serious issues are:

1. applying the general warranty regime to title, capacity and potentially every other claim;
2. no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct;
3. inadequate Bluefen and Riverlark completion protection;
4. broad deemed disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions;
5. omission of the employee bonuses and on-costs from funds flow; and
6. treating unresolved Tax and IP positions as settled.

The Disclosure Letter is nevertheless helpful in confirming that Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay title and the DD-006 investigation remain unresolved. Those disclosures should drive completion protections, not merely eliminate Buyer claims.

## Detailed departures and recommended pushback

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Playbook:** 25%, or AUD 6 million. The 20% fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the relevant draft. No authority has been given.

**Pushback:** Restore the general warranty cap to **AUD 6 million**. We cannot accept or describe AUD 4.8 million as agreed without Amelia’s draft-specific written approval.

The cap must apply only to clearly defined **General Warranty Claims**, not title, Tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenant claims.

---

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- AUD 250,000 basket; and
- only loss above the basket is recoverable.

**Playbook:**

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar—a tipping basket.

**Pushback:** Replace the Seller’s thresholds with the playbook position. The Seller proposal is materially more restrictive in three ways: each claim must be five times larger, aggregate valid claims must reach five times the agreed target, and the first AUD 250,000 would never be recoverable.

The thresholds must not apply to title/fundamental claims, specific indemnities, fraud-related matters, payment obligations or covenant breaches.

---

### 3. General claim period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Playbook:** 24 months. An 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

**Pushback:** Restore **24 months**. Also reject the proposal that any limitation applies to “all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.” Each liability category should have its own express regime.

Any claims procedure should preserve a claim on reasonably detailed notice; it should not require final quantification before the notification deadline.

---

### 4. Fundamental, title and capacity claims

**Seller position:** Same cap and time limit as general warranties.

**Playbook:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general de minimis, basket and knowledge bar.

**Pushback:** Require:

- a **100% of purchase price cap**;
- at least a **six-year claims period**;
- no general de minimis or basket;
- no Buyer-knowledge defence;
- separate treatment for ownership, title, capacity, authority and absence of encumbrances.

A Buyer acquiring 100% of the Company must not bear the risk that the Seller lacks title or authority to sell merely because the issue emerges after 18 months or exceeds a 20% cap.

---

### 5. Fraud and misconduct carve-outs

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims of any nature. No relevant carve-out is offered.

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This position cannot be waived.

**Pushback:** Add an overriding carve-out applying across the agreement. It should prevail over clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and any other limitation, disclosure, knowledge or remedies language.

The phrase “all Claims of any nature” is unacceptable because it could also pull title, indemnity, covenant and payment claims into the general regime.

---

### 6. Disclosure standard

**Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records.

**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Pushback:** Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. A matter should qualify a warranty only where it is:

- specifically disclosed against the relevant warranty;
- described with sufficient detail to identify its nature and reasonably apparent scope; and
- supported by clearly identified documents.

Public availability, mere inclusion in the data room, or the possibility that advisers could discover something should not constitute disclosure.

The Seller’s specific disclosures can be assessed individually. Some identify genuine facts, but they should not automatically qualify every warranty or eliminate contractual completion obligations.

Paragraph 1.4 may operate as a general reservation against an evidentiary admission, but it must not override the SPA, negate warranties or conditions, or prevent the disclosed facts from triggering agreed remedies.

---

### 7. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.

**Playbook:** Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions. They must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Pushback:** Delete clause 8.3 in its proposed form. “Discoverable” information is constructive knowledge, not actual knowledge, and would recreate the rejected whole-data-room disclosure standard.

If any limited knowledge concept is ultimately retained, it should be confined to actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer deal-team individuals, without imputation from advisers and without a duty to investigate. It must not apply to:

- title, ownership, capacity or authority;
- fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct;
- a specific indemnity;
- payment obligations or covenants; or
- matters the Seller is required to cure before Completion.

Separately, any Seller warranty qualified by Seller knowledge should use named Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.

---

### 8. Bluefen consent

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied upon delivery of written consent.

**Diligence position:** Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, around 30%. No final consent or evidence that its associated conditions have been satisfied is presently included.

**Playbook:** Effective consent and evidence that all conditions are satisfied before Completion.

**Pushback:** Bluefen should remain a substantive condition precedent requiring, before Completion:

1. final, effective written consent from the correct counterparty;
2. satisfaction or valid waiver of all conditions under clause 11.3;
3. evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer; and
4. no adverse amendment, fee, termination right or other material condition unless accepted by the Buyer.

Delivery alone is insufficient if the consent is conditional or ineffective. Reasonable endeavours should not replace the required outcome. Completion by the Buyer should not inadvertently waive the condition unless the Buyer gives an express written waiver.

---

### 9. Riverlark facility and security

**Seller position:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million outstanding; release after Completion.

**Playbook:** Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval.

**Pushback:** Require:

- an up-to-date payout letter;
- direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds;
- confirmation that the facility is fully discharged;
- effective releases of all Company and asset security at Completion; and
- appropriate registration discharge evidence.

The Buyer should not acquire the Company while the Seller’s debt remains secured over it. If the Seller insists on a post-Completion administrative release, it must provide a satisfactory irrevocable bank undertaking, and the structure cannot be accepted without Amelia’s written approval.

The treatment must also be consistent with the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

---

### 10. Employee Completion bonuses

**Seller position:** AUD 420,000 is “a matter for the Seller” but is not separately itemised in the funds flow.

**Diligence position:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and continued employment. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs remain unidentified.

**Playbook:** Specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently omit them.

**Pushback:** Require the Completion statement and funds flow expressly to show:

- the AUD 420,000 bonuses;
- all applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs;
- who is legally responsible for paying them; and
- how they are funded.

If Company funds will be used after Completion, the amount should be funded by the Seller or otherwise expressly reflected in the price mechanics. A statement that the amounts are a Seller matter is inadequate unless backed by payment mechanics and an enforceable obligation preventing cost leakage to the Buyer.

---

### 11. Ironquay IP

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment.

**Diligence position:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independent verification of non-payment. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is included.

**Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified.

**Pushback:** Require a completion cure comprising:

- verification of the actual amount payable;
- payment from Seller funds or expressly through the funds flow;
- receipt confirming cleared payment;
- effective assignment or confirmation of ownership of all relevant Project Materials and IP rights; and
- evidence that no lien, retention right or further fee remains.

The indemnity should cover all losses arising from the failure to obtain valid ownership or use rights, outstanding amounts, enforcement by Ironquay and the cost of obtaining replacement or confirmatory rights. It should not be confined merely to paying the stated SOW3 invoice.

Do not stipulate that AUD 180,000 is either definitively due or not due until independently verified.

---

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Disclosure:** A link was sent to an unintended external email address and may contain approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and notification obligations remain unestablished. No confirmed breach or loss amount is stated.

**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates, while making no unsupported assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or quantum.

**Pushback:** Require pre-Completion covenants to:

- preserve all relevant logs, devices, communications and evidence;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- give the Buyer prompt and regular updates;
- provide investigation materials and relevant expert advice;
- consult the Buyer before external notification or material remediation, where legally permissible; and
- comply with applicable legal obligations.

The SPA and disclosure should remain neutral on whether there has been unauthorised access, a notifiable breach, loss or material harm. We should not accept the Seller’s unsupported “not material” conclusion, but equally should not assert a confirmed breach or numeric claim without evidence.

---

### 13. Sandbar renewals

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Disclosure:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, but it does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Pushback:** Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods, payment status and accounting treatment. Test whether the commitments are ordinary-course expenses, accruals, prepayments, leakage or another price-mechanics item.

Do not automatically classify the AUD 330,000 as Debt or deduct it from price. Equally, do not accept the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation without analysis.

---

### 14. Tax and IP regime

**Seller position:** Treated as settled under the general regime.

**Playbook:** Tax and IP remain open; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.

**Pushback:** State expressly that neither regime is agreed. Do not allow the general 20%/18-month regime to resolve them by implication.

Tax, IP, title, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities should remain separately identified. Their caps, periods, thresholds and remedies require express negotiation. We should not presently concede unlimited liability, but nor should we accept the Seller’s proposed general limitations.

---

### 15. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves title to 100% of the shares.

**Playbook:** Require independent ownership, title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is only a supplied internal source.

**Pushback:** Require, as applicable:

- original or verified share certificates;
- ASIC and PPSR searches;
- constitutional and shareholder records;
- board and shareholder approvals;
- evidence of the chain of title;
- confirmation of issued capital and absence of options or other rights;
- releases of any security over the shares; and
- appropriate completion transfers and officer certificates.

The register is relevant evidence but is maintained by or for the Company and is not independent proof of beneficial ownership, lack of encumbrances or Seller authority.

---

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures currently say only that:

- the office lease has a notification obligation, not necessarily a consent requirement; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment, without expressly applying to a share sale.

We should verify the complete clauses but should not manufacture consent conditions unsupported by the contracts. If only notice is required, require timely and contractually compliant notice. If no change-of-control provision exists, Mossvale consent should not be demanded merely because there is an assignment restriction.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. Reinstate the **AUD 6 million general warranty cap**, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket and 24-month period.
2. Establish a separate **100% / six-year minimum** title and fundamental regime, outside thresholds and knowledge limitations.
3. Insert the mandatory overriding carve-out for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**.
4. Delete whole-data-room and public-record disclosure and the constructive Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
5. Make effective **Bluefen consent**, including satisfaction of its conditions, a genuine condition precedent.
6. Require current **Riverlark payout and releases at Completion**, with direct repayment from Completion funds.
7. Itemise and Seller-fund the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all triggered on-costs**.
8. Broaden and operationalise the **Ironquay cure and indemnity**, without assuming the unverified AUD 180,000 figure is conclusive.
9. Impose evidence-preservation, investigation and reporting obligations for **DD-006**, without asserting a confirmed breach or loss.
10. Investigate the **Sandbar renewals** without automatically treating them as Debt.
11. Keep **Tax, IP, title, payment, covenant and indemnity claims** separate and expressly negotiated.
12. Obtain independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence rather than relying solely on DD-012.

None of the Seller’s proposed 20% cap or 18-month period should be accepted without Amelia Frost’s prior written, draft-specific approval.

**Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment.

**Diligence position:** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but this is not independent verification of non-payment. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is included.

**Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified.

**Pushback:** Require a completion cure comprising:

- verification of the actual amount payable;
- payment from Seller funds or expressly through the funds flow;
- receipt confirming cleared payment;
- effective assignment or confirmation of ownership of all relevant Project Materials and IP rights; and
- evidence that no lien, retention right or further fee remains.

The indemnity should cover all losses arising from the failure to obtain valid ownership or use rights, outstanding amounts, enforcement by Ironquay and the cost of obtaining replacement or confirmatory rights. It should not be confined merely to paying the stated SOW3 invoice.

Do not stipulate that AUD 180,000 is either definitively due or not due until independently verified.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Seller position:** Preliminary and not expected to be material.

**Disclosure:** A link was sent to an unintended external email address and may contain approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and notification obligations remain unestablished. No confirmed breach or loss amount is stated.

**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates, while making no unsupported assumption of breach, harm, notification duty or quantum.

**Pushback:** Require pre-Completion covenants to:

- preserve all relevant logs, devices, communications and evidence;
- continue a properly scoped investigation;
- give the Buyer prompt and regular updates;
- provide investigation materials and relevant expert advice;
- consult the Buyer before external notification or material remediation, where legally permissible; and
- comply with applicable legal obligations.

The SPA and disclosure should remain neutral on whether there has been unauthorised access, a notifiable breach, loss or material harm. We should not accept the Seller’s unsupported “not material” conclusion, but equally should not assert a confirmed breach or numeric claim without evidence.

### 13. Sandbar renewals

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Disclosure:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, but it does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Pushback:** Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights, service periods, payment status and accounting treatment. Test whether the commitments are ordinary-course expenses, accruals, prepayments, leakage or another price-mechanics item.

Do not automatically classify the AUD 330,000 as Debt or deduct it from price. Equally, do not accept the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation without analysis.

### 14. Tax and IP regime

**Seller position:** Treated as settled under the general regime.

**Playbook:** Tax and IP remain open; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution.

**Pushback:** State expressly that neither regime is agreed. Do not allow the general 20%/18-month regime to resolve them by implication.

Tax, IP, title, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities should remain separately identified. Their caps, periods, thresholds and remedies require express negotiation. We should not presently concede unlimited liability, but nor should we accept the Seller’s proposed general limitations.

### 15. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register proves title to 100% of the shares.

**Playbook:** Require independent ownership, title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is only a supplied internal source.

**Pushback:** Require, as applicable:

- original or verified share certificates;
- ASIC and PPSR searches;
- constitutional and shareholder records;
- board and shareholder approvals;
- evidence of the chain of title;
- confirmation of issued capital and absence of options or other rights;
- releases of any security over the shares; and
- appropriate completion transfers and officer certificates.

The register is relevant evidence but is maintained by or for the Company and is not independent proof of beneficial ownership, lack of encumbrances or Seller authority.

### 16. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosures currently say only that:

- the office lease has a notification obligation, not necessarily a consent requirement; and
- Mossvale restricts assignment, without expressly applying to a share sale.

We should verify the complete clauses but should not manufacture consent conditions unsupported by the contracts. If only notice is required, require timely and contractually compliant notice. If no change-of-control provision exists, Mossvale consent should not be demanded merely because there is an assignment restriction.

## Recommended negotiating position

1. Reinstate the **AUD 6 million general warranty cap**, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket and 24-month period.
2. Establish a separate **100% / six-year minimum** title and fundamental regime, outside thresholds and knowledge limitations.
3. Insert the mandatory overriding carve-out for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**.
4. Delete whole-data-room and public-record disclosure and the constructive Buyer-knowledge exclusion.
5. Make effective **Bluefen consent**, including satisfaction of its conditions, a genuine condition precedent.
6. Require current **Riverlark payout and releases at Completion**, with direct repayment from Completion funds.
7. Itemise and Seller-fund the **AUD 420,000 bonuses plus all triggered on-costs**.
8. Broaden and operationalise the **Ironquay cure and indemnity**, without assuming the unverified AUD 180,000 figure is conclusive.
9. Impose evidence-preservation, investigation and reporting obligations for **DD-006**, without asserting a confirmed breach or loss.
10. Investigate the **Sandbar renewals** without automatically treating them as Debt.
11. Keep **Tax, IP, title, payment, covenant and indemnity claims** separate and expressly negotiated.
12. Obtain independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence rather than relying solely on DD-012.

None of the Seller’s proposed 20% cap or 18-month period should be accepted without Amelia Frost’s prior written, draft-specific approval.
